problem:
Find the Laplace transform $Y(s)=L{y(t)}$ for $s>2$ if 

$$
{y}^{′}-2y=-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,y(0)=1.
$$

You may make use of the following result:

$$
L{\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t}=\frac{\omega }{{s}^{2}+{\omega }^{2}},\,s>0.
$$
worked_solution:
First, we take the Laplace transform of both sides and use the addition and scalar multiplication properties of the Laplace transform:

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{y}^{′}-2y} & =L{-5\operatorname{sin}⁡t} \\ L{{y}^{′}}-2L{y} & =-5L{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate $L{{y}^{′}},$ we use the formula for the Laplace transform of a derivative and the initial condition $y(0)=1:$

$$
L{{y}^{′}}=sL{y}-y(0)=sY(s)-1
$$

From the table of Laplace transforms, we have the following result:

$$
L{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}=\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1},\,s>0
$$

Therefore, we can solve for $Y(s):$

$$
\begin{aligned}L{{y}^{′}}-2L{y} & =-5L{\operatorname{sin}⁡t} \\ (sY(s)-1)-2Y(s) & =-5(\frac{1}{{s}^{2}+1}) \\ sY(s)-2Y(s) & =1-\frac{5}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ (s-2)Y(s) & =\frac{{s}^{2}-4}{{s}^{2}+1} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{{s}^{2}-4}{({s}^{2}+1)(s-2)}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $s>2,$ we simplify as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}Y(s) & =\frac{(s-2)(s+2)}{({s}^{2}+1)(s-2)} \\ Y(s) & =\frac{s+2}{{s}^{2}+1}\end{aligned}
$$
